title: Given a single positive integer N, draw a flowchart to print all even integers between 1 and N inclusive. Start, read N, initialize i = 2, loop while i <= N doing print i and i = i + 2, End. Alternatively loop i from 1 to N and print i only when i % 2 == 0. Input: 10, Expected Output: 2 4 6 8 10.
shortTitle: Print Even Numbers: print all even integers between 1 and N
keyPoints: The stepping approach starts at 2 and increments by 2, only ever touching even numbers: N/2 iterations, no modulo test.
The filter approach loops from 1 to N and prints only when i % 2 == 0: twice the iterations and a modulo check each.
The stepping approach is more efficient and simpler to reason about for fixed-stride generation.
The filter approach is better when the selection rule is more complex than a fixed stride.
For N < 2, the result is empty because there are no even numbers in that range.
In production, collect values into a list and return it rather than printing, for testability.

s1_definition.oneliner: Print evens by starting at 2 and stepping by 2 up to N: more efficient than walking all numbers and filtering with modulo.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Stepping approach** – start at 2, increment by 2: `for (int i = 2; i <= n; i += 2)`. Only touches evens.
- **Filter approach** – loop 1 to N, print when `i % 2 == 0`. Double the iterations.
- **Efficiency** – stepping does N/2 iterations with no test; filter does N iterations with a modulo each.
- **Empty result** – for N < 2, no even numbers exist in range.
- **Testability** – collect into a list and return rather than printing.
s1_definition.analogy: National Bank of India schedules an audit of even-numbered accounts up to account N. The system lists 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 for N = 10, stepping by two so it never wastes time on odd accounts.

sections.s6_takeaway:
Printing the even numbers up to N is best done with a stepping approach: start at 2, increment by 2, and collect each value. This only touches even numbers and does about N/2 iterations with no per-element test. The filter approach loops from 1 to N and checks each with modulo, doing twice the work, but is useful when the selection rule is more complex.

For N less than 2, the result is empty because there are no even numbers in that range. Collecting into a list and returning it rather than printing makes the method testable and composable.

In a banking project at National Bank of India, even-numbered accounts were selected for an audit worklist up to a cutoff. The stepping loop produced the list efficiently, and the returned collection was passed to the next processing stage.

Remember one sentence: start at 2 and step by 2 to generate only evens, avoiding the overhead of checking every number with modulo.
